blocks.h2: What to Do During a Sewage Backup
blocks.intro: A sewage backup is a health risk as much as a plumbing problem. Here's what to do while we're on the way:

steps.body: Don't flush, run the dishwasher or do laundry. Every gallon that goes down a drain has nowhere to go but back up.
Sewage carries bacteria. Keep everyone out of the affected area and don't try to clean it with bare hands.
Our phone line is open around the clock, including weekends and holidays. Tell us which drains are backing up and we'll take it from there.

blocks.h2: Why Sewage Backs Up Into a Home
blocks.intro: Most backups come down to one of a few causes. The camera tells us which one you have:

tiles.body: Roots grow into older pipe at the joints and build a net that catches everything else. On tree-lined Highland Park lots, this is the most common cause we'd check first.
Grease, wipes and scale narrow the pipe over time until one day nothing gets through.
A cracked clay joint or a belly in the line lets waste collect until it backs up. That calls for a [sewer repair](/highland-park/sewer-repair), not just a cleaning.
If your basement bathroom or laundry drains through an [ejector pump](/highland-park/ejector-pump), a failed pump can back up sewage even when the main line is clear.

blocks.h2: Sewage Backups in Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: The median home in Highland Park was built in 1963, and nearly half were built before 1960. Older clay lines and mature trees are the combination behind most backups here.

items.body: In Highland Park, the homeowner owns and maintains the private sewer line from the house to the city main. A backup that starts in that line is yours to fix, so an accurate diagnosis saves money.

Once the line is clear, the fix that lasts depends on the cause: [hydro jetting](/highland-park/hydro-jetting) for roots and buildup, a repair for broken pipe, or an [overhead sewer system](/highland-park/overhead-sewer-systems) for a connection that can't keep up in heavy rain. The city's flood tips also recommend backflow preventers.
Call a licensed plumber before a cleanup crew. If sewage is still coming in, the source has to be stopped before any cleanup is effective. We stop it, then restoration can begin.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: When sewage is in your basement, you need a plumber who shows up and explains what's going on, not a sales pitch.

steps.body: We run a camera down the line and show you what we see, in plain language.
We walk you through your options, short-term and long-term, and tell you which one we'd pick for your line.
You get a flat rate before any money changes hands.

blocks.h2: Sewage Backup Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Who do I call when sewage backs up into my basement?
items.preview: A licensed plumber first, to stop the source. Cleanup comes after.
items.answer: Call a licensed plumber first. If sewage is still coming in, the source needs to be stopped before any cleanup is effective. We clear the line, find the cause on camera and fix it. Once it's stopped, restoration can begin.

items.q: Is a sewage backup the city's responsibility in Highland Park?
items.preview: Usually not. Most backups start in the private line the homeowner owns.
items.answer: Usually not. In Highland Park, the homeowner owns and maintains the private sewer line from the house to the city main, and most basement backups start with a blockage in that line. The camera shows where the blockage is.

items.q: How do I keep sewage from backing up again?
items.preview: It depends on the cause: cleaning, repair, a backflow valve or an overhead sewer.
items.answer: Start with the cause. Roots and buildup call for [hydro jetting](/highland-park/hydro-jetting) and [regular maintenance](/highland-park/sewer-maintenance). Broken pipe calls for a repair. A connection that backs up in heavy rain may need a backflow valve or an overhead sewer system. We'll tell you which one fits your home.

items.q: How much does it cost to fix a sewage backup?
items.preview: It depends on the cause. You get a flat-rate price before any work begins.
items.answer: It depends on what's causing it: a clog that clears with rodding is a different job than a broken line or a failed ejector pump. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in.
